key_insight: Across high-quartile medical journals, evaluative stance toward medical AI shifted toward more scrutiny from 2021 to 2026, while cautious optimism remained the dominant tone.
clinical_relevance: This suggests the medical literature is increasingly emphasizing AI safety, failure modes, and oversight rather than only performance gains.
method: LLM-assisted content analysis of 97,492 Q1/Q2 medical journal records from 2021-Apr 2026
16,759 discourse/evaluative abstracts retained; 16,749 valid stance labels assigned
Validated against blinded human coding for prefiltering, stance, specialty, and failure-mechanism axes
evidence_signal: Among 16,749 valid classifications, 30.8% were critical (Alarm/Caution), with critical share rising from 25.4% to 32.6% over the study period.
watch_item: Moderate agreement for failure-mode coding means fabrication/error estimates should be interpreted cautiously and may overstate precision.
paper_title: Evaluative Stance Toward Artificial Intelligence in High-Quartile Medical Journals (2021-2026): Large-Scale LLM-Assisted Computational Content Analysis
